title: Spatial group discovery
summary: Find groups of spots that are both similar in expression and physically clumped, and pair each against the rest of its split.

third_party.name: julia
third_party.note: Read from the image. Manifest.toml records 1.9.0, so the lockfile and the runtime disagree; the image is what executes. The RNG stream is a language guarantee, so this matters under a fixed seed.

third_party.name: SpectralInference.jl
third_party.note: Supplies the singular value decomposition and the spectral distance between spots. The entire tree derives from this.

third_party.name: Noise.jl
third_party.note: Backs the multiplicative Gaussian perturbation used to build replicate trees.

third_party.name: spatstat.explore
third_party.note: Supplies the border corrected Ripley's K. Modern spatstat is split into several packages and Kest lives here.

third_party.name: booster (installed as gotree)
third_party.note: The binary at /usr/local/bin/gotree self identifies as booster, a different tool with a different command line. It is committed to this repository at bin/gotree, sha256 c1984a89b66b625045178fcbc1ed653f55d0f8c4802ce4cdd673c4cea4ea3dd2, which makes it the best pinned dependency here. It also fails to start unless LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes /lib64, because singularity replaces the library path and libgomp is not found.

third_party.name: phangorn
third_party.note: Descendant and sibling lookups during pair construction.

environment.provenance: Digest read from the build on randi dated 2026-07-02. The recipe cannot regenerate it: build_r_container.sh resolves CRAN against 'latest' rather than a dated snapshot, so this file is currently the only record of the versions below.

inputs.name: positions
inputs.description: Spot coordinates. The millimetre columns drive every spatial decision.

outputs.name: tree
outputs.description: The pruned tree whose surviving nodes are the spatial groups.

outputs.name: sg_pairs
outputs.description: One row per comparison: a dominant node against the pooled remainder of its split.

outputs.name: sg_pair_members
outputs.description: Which spots belong to each side of each pair.

outputs.name: node_info
outputs.description: Per surviving node: its size, support and spatial statistic. Declared because the cohort analysis reads it. It was always produced and always copied into optimal/, but naming it here is what makes it something this capability promises rather than something a later step happens to find.

outputs.name: node_leaves
outputs.description: Spots beneath every node. Consumed by growchain.

outputs.name: node_parents
outputs.description: Ancestor chain per node. Consumed by growchain.

outputs.name: chosen_svd
outputs.description: Which candidate size was selected, and its score. Its header carries the wall clock time it was written, which is excluded from the digest so that two identical runs still compare equal.

parameters.name: svd_values
parameters.description: Candidate SVD sizes to sweep. The repository uses [5, 50, 150] for a fast run and thirty values from 5 to 150 for production. Stages 1 to 6 repeat once per value, so the length of this list is the single parameter deciding whether a scheduler is needed.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: A label the tree building kernel requires. It names the run in log output and does not enter any computation.

parameters.name: num_boot
parameters.description: Replicate trees built by perturbing the matrix. Drives branch support.

parameters.name: support_threshold
parameters.description: Branch support below which a node is collapsed during pruning.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Makes the replicate perturbation and the hyperparameter search reproducible. Left unset in production runs.

stages.title: Build the tree and its replicates
stages.template: sh -c 'for b in $(seq 0 {num_boot}); do julia --project=kernels/tumorspace_core/julia {entrypoint} --dataset {dataset} --input-dir {data_dir} --output-dir {run_dir} --svd-value {item} --svd-run {run} --boot $b {when_seeded} || exit 1; done'
stages.seed_note: This kernel does not read TUMORSPACE_FIXED_SEED. It seeds the replicate perturbation only when --test-seed or --test is present, from offset + svd_run*100 + boot*1000, and otherwise draws unseeded. The value after --test-seed supplies the offset; a bare flag keeps the historical 1000, so an unvalued run reproduces every number it always produced. Passed only when a seed was supplied, leaving an unseeded run exactly as it was. The offsets are strided 100 against 1000, so eleven or more svd_values makes run 11 boot 0 collide with run 1 boot 1; the wrapper refuses that configuration rather than renumbering, which would change every number the default path produces.
stages.memory_hint: Holds a spot by spot distance matrix, so memory grows with the square of the spot count.
stages.note: Uses named arguments, unlike every other stage here. Builds num_boot+1 trees per candidate size: replicate 0 is the original and the rest are perturbed. The fan out is therefore two dimensional, candidate size by replicate.

seed_capacity.because: the derived seed is offset + svd_run*100 + boot*1000, so run 11 at bootstrap 0 lands on the same seed as run 1 at bootstrap 1

stages.title: Branch support
stages.template: sh -c 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/julia/lib/julia:/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH; rm -f {run_dir}/Tree_Bootstrap.nw; for i in $(seq 1 {num_boot}); do cat {run_dir}/Tree_$i.nw >> {run_dir}/Tree_Bootstrap.nw; done; gotree -i {run_dir}/Tree_0.nw -b {run_dir}/Tree_Bootstrap.nw -o {run_dir}/Tree_support.nw -@ 4 -a tbe'
stages.note: Transfer bootstrap expectation against the replicate trees; stage 5 refuses to run without its output. Two things here are not what they look like. The binary is booster rather than gotree, so the command line is -i/-b/-o/-a rather than a gotree subcommand. And it will not start unless the library path is set inside the container, which is why the command is wrapped in sh.

stages.title: Extract node structure
stages.memory_hint: One of the two stages the orchestrator raises to 128 GB above 8000 spots.
stages.note: The only kernel here with no function boundary at all, so wrapping it requires lifting math out of a script body first.

stages.title: Spatial clumping per node
stages.note: An R stage inside an otherwise Julia chain. Replaced a slower Julia implementation.

stages.title: Spatial optimisation
stages.seed_note: A random search over three hyperparameters. Unseeded, it selects a different setting each run, which changes the pruning and therefore every downstream result. This is the largest single source of run to run variability in the pipeline.
stages.memory_hint: The second stage raised to 128 GB above 8000 spots.
stages.note: The bespoke heart. Scores each draw by how well the surviving nodes reconstruct the tissue geography.

stages.title: Collapse weakly supported nodes
stages.note: Collapsing rather than deleting is what creates multi way splits, which the pairing stage then has to handle.

stages.title: Choose the candidate size
stages.note: The repository has no callable form of this step: the selection lives inside a heredoc that run_svd_selection.sh writes out and submits with sbatch, so it cannot be reached from inside an allocation. kernels/ holds a verbatim copy with the placeholders turned into arguments; its header records the source lines and the one changed default. It is pure housekeeping with no scientific dependency, so it runs on the host rather than in an image. The one external tool it needs is bc, for the floating point comparison that picks the winning candidate.

stages.title: Form the region pairs
stages.note: Designates the branch with the most leaves as the node and pools every other sibling against it. Produces the handoff that every downstream capability consumes.

determinism.note: Two stages draw from the RNG, and they take a seed by different routes. optimise reads TUMORSPACE_FIXED_SEED and honours the value. tree_build ignores that variable and takes its offset as an argument instead, which the wrapper supplies only when a seed was given. Measured: without that argument, two runs seeded identically diverge at Tree_support.nw, because the replicate trees were never seeded, and every later artifact inherits it.

resources.scales_with: spots squared, multiplied by the number of candidate SVD sizes
resources.memory_hint: 32 GB below 3000 spots, 64 GB below 8000, 128 GB above, applied to node_extract and optimise. The other stages are flat.

notes: The per candidate hyperparameter search table, cor_dat_all.tsv, is written into every svd_run_N directory and is what the selection step reads to pick a winner. It is not among the files that step copies into optimal/, so once the working tree is cleared the evidence for why one setting won is gone. Only the winner's identity survives, in optimal_svd.txt. This contract does not declare it as an output because there is no fixed path at which it exists after the run; recovering it means keeping the staging tree.
interpretation:
Region identifiers are internal to one sample. The same number in another sample is an unrelated region, so they must never be compared across samples and must not be used as a key to join two samples together.

A region count on its own says nothing. A tumour often splits into many boundaries that separate one gene or none, alongside a few that separate hundreds, so what identifies a sample's real internal divisions is the ranking by how many features actually separate a region from its neighbour. Balance is how evenly a split divides its spots: 0.5 is even, and a small value means a sliver against the rest.
for_people: Finds groups of spots that are alike in expression and sit together in the tissue, and pairs each against the rest of its split.
